question: Does the publisher-indexed full Silliman article text clarify access and add any additional fish that can be assigned to Paitan Lake from the previously flattened table excerpts?

source.title: Endemic, Indigenous, and Introduced Species in the Freshwater Ecosystems of Nueva Ecija and Pampanga: Status, Diversity, and Impacts
source.citation: Paz-Alberto, A. M., Castro, E. S., Flores, V. L., & Romero, M. A. V. (2009). Silliman Journal, 50(2), 43-60.

access.result: On 2026-11-19 the publisher-hosted PDF became queryable as an 856-line full-text document through the web search index. Relevant methods, site-list, tables, and discussion sections were opened directly from that indexed document. Direct PDF fetch and PDF screenshot still returned HTTP 502; no local article copy was obtained.
reviewedSections: Methods and study area list: indexed lines 112-153
Nueva Ecija sampling-site legend: indexed lines 158-163
limitations: The full document is queryable in the publisher search index, but direct PDF retrieval and page screenshots remain unavailable in this review environment.
The table text extraction flattens row and site-column positions. Only a Paitan assignment that is explicit in prose or has a clearly legible site-column relationship is retained.
The article does not supply verified fish field dates, station coordinates, specimen vouchers, or a Paitan-specific accession crosswalk.

studyDesign.reportedSampling: The article describes three designated stations for each Nueva Ecija study area and ten randomly selected 10 m by 12 m quadrats per station.
studyDesign.identificationNote: The article says identifications were authenticated by fisheries technologists at CLSU and NFRDI and a National Museum taxonomist. This review did not independently inspect vouchers or specimen-to-station data.

paitanFishCandidates.waterbodyLink: The discussion explicitly names Paitan Lake, Cuyapo, among the sites where the fish was recorded in the study.
paitanFishCandidates.tableCrossCheck: Table 1 includes the taxon in the Nueva Ecija site table; no SIV value is transcribed here.
paitanFishCandidates.temporalScope: Historical study; field collection dates are not verified.
paitanFishCandidates.disposition: Historical source-reported Paitan candidate only. The 2026 Catalog of Fishes name check does not re-identify the studied specimen or establish current presence.

paitanFishCandidates.waterbodyLink: Table 3 headings name Paitan Lake, and its Oreochromis niloticus row contains a value in that site column in the publisher-indexed text.
paitanFishCandidates.temporalScope: Historical study; field collection dates are not verified.
paitanFishCandidates.disposition: Historical source-reported Paitan candidate only. The 2026 Catalog of Fishes name check does not re-identify the studied specimen or establish current presence.

additionalFishDisposition.result: No additional Nueva Ecija fish name was assigned to Paitan from the flattened Table 1 or Table 3 extraction.
additionalFishDisposition.reason: Other fish names are reported for the Nueva Ecija study as a whole, but their row-to-Paitan column links are not sufficiently legible in the indexed text. No locality assignment is inferred from presence elsewhere in the study or from numeric values without a reliable column position.

rightsAndUse.status: The issue states author and journal copyright and all rights reserved; no item-specific reuse permission was identified.
rightsAndUse.retainedMaterial: No PDF, screenshot, table image, figure, SIV value, or verbatim article passage is retained. This artifact records only concise attributed research findings and access conditions.

nextStep: Continue separate Vaca Dam Reservoir and Central Luzon freshwater source research. For Paitan, seek an independently dated survey or specimen/voucher record and item-specific reuse guidance; do not infer current presence from this historical study.
